public_work.name: ypi
public_work.what: A recursive coding agent built on Pi. A single `rlm_query` tool spawns child agents with the same prompt and tools, isolated in jj workspaces, with five guardrails: depth, call count, dollar budget, timeout and PATH scrubbing. It includes a `make doctor` and parity tests.

public_work.name: OpenProse
public_work.what: A Markdown 'language' executed inside the agent session: responsibilities declare Requires/Maintains contracts and are wired by the model. His PR #62 added deterministic skill declarations, and he wrote the auto-pocock example.

public_work.name: Skill Safety Data Sheet (SSDS)
public_work.what: An open standard (v0.2.0) that rates agent skills on Host/Data/Actuation/Content hazards (0-4). Hazard flags are derived deterministically from a capability manifest, including prompt-injection surfaces, then mapped to containment levels and required approvals. It has a Zod schema with sha256 artifact pinning.

public_work.name: LongCoT / StudyBench harness experiments
public_work.what: Reports Codex CLI with gpt-5.5 xhigh at 1446/1995 (72.5%) on full LongCoT, against the paper's claim that math and chemistry stay near zero. StudyBench library/lab ablations are published with their environments.

public_work.name: rlm-cli
public_work.what: A CLI wrapper for RLM with directory-as-context and JSON-first output.

relevance.why: Several MIT artifacts sit squarely in our lanes: a bounded recursive agent (ypi), a Rust budgeted repo index with a hook integration (dirpack), and a contract-style agent workflow language (OpenProse). SSDS is a ready-made hazard rubric for vetting skills. His 'it's the harness, not the model' benchmark method matches franken-research's evidence grading.

study_next.what: Map SSDS HDAC scoring and hazard flags onto our skill intake and security scan
study_next.why: It gives a deterministic hazard score and required approvals for each skill, which complements our own skill security scan and hook certification.

study_next.what: Benchmark dirpack against our orientation tools on one Rust repo
study_next.why: A Rust, MIT, fixed-token-budget index with a SessionStart hook; measure the token savings on our own repositories and on Jeffrey's crates.

study_next.what: Study ypi's guardrails (depth, budget, call cap, jj isolation) for bounded subagent recursion
study_next.why: Directly comparable to how OMP and NTM bound fan-out; the parity tests are a model for harness compatibility gates.
